source.title: Genesis: Visual Augmentation Primitives for Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
source.authors: Fan Yang; Lifeng Chen; Yipu Wang; Han Wang; Feilong Chen; Yidong Ma; Zhiyang Chen; Chaoyang Zhao; Lingxiang Wu; Hanqi Jiang; Yibo Chen; Xu Tang; Yao Hu; Ming Tang; Xiaojie Jin; Xiaolong Zheng; Jinqiao Wang

record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream performance across model sizes in visual reasoning and VQA, a multimodal setting; it does not measure the text-pretraining loss or fit the original scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper reports cross-entropy losses, parameter/token/compute sweeps, extrapolation fits, compute-optimal allocations, or architecture-shape comparisons for none of the claim versions. Its Genesis benchmark scores across model sizes bear on V6. Table 1's ZeroBench entries and Table 3's Genesis rows are not reliably assignable to models or metrics from the flattened layout, so they are not recorded as rows. Cited scaling-law discussion and the paper's own scaling-law characterization are not independent measured results.
record.test_reason: Weak T3 test of V6 only. The study reports downstream benchmark scores for its RL-trained Genesis models at three sizes (4B, 8B, 32B), and the authors say this validates 'the scaling law for visual reasoning.' The size variation comes from three different Qwen3-VL base checkpoints, with different batch sizes and compute. There are only three points and no fitted curve, loss measure or extrapolation. So the data shows only whether scores rise with size, not whether they rise predictably.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that Genesis-4B beats 8B baselines and that performance improves consistently up to 32B, and they explicitly call this 'validating the scaling law for visual reasoning.' They acknowledge validation only on Qwen3-VL sizes, a 600-sample UNREAL benchmark and possible judge noise. They fit no laws. Their 'consistent improvement over baselines' claim is not fully accurate: Genesis-32B falls below its base on MathVista (−0.5), BabyVision (−1.6) and HallusionBench (−0.4).
record.recipe_differences: This is multimodal model training and benchmark evaluation across three sizes, not the original text-only held-out cross-entropy scaling experiments or compute-optimal allocation analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Benchmark changes the observed trend: BabyVision declines with size and LogicVista dips from 4B to 8B.
record.code_released: not stated; the paper says models, data, and code will be publicly released
record.peer_reviewed: Accepted to the EMNLP 2026 Main Conference
record.problems: Only Qwen3-VL configurations at 4B, 8B, and 32B are used for Genesis. The reported outcomes are benchmark scores rather than pretraining losses, and there are no fitted scaling curves or extrapolation tests. The paper notes a 600-sample UNREAL benchmark and possible noise from its LLM-based rubric judge. Some flattened table entries cannot be reliably assigned.
record.rows_left_out: ZeroBench rows from Table 1 and Genesis results from Table 3 are omitted because the flattened layout does not support reliable assignment of all values to models and metrics. No results beyond the 30 clearly assignable benchmark scores are left out.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss or power-law fit.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
No power-law form fitted for the multimodal or RL regime.
Predictability (no fitted trend or forecast), relation to pretraining loss, and scaling isolated from base-model differences.

missing.what: Genesis UNREAL overall scores 14.2/19.1/25.7 (4B/8B/32B), readable via subscripts against Qwen3-VL 12.8/17.5/24.3. Sub-scores: Math 6.1/8.9/18.9, Nat.Sci 32.3/40.3/37.1, Percep 14.1/20.7/29.4, Phys 15.7/28.4/26.5, Reas 24.7/23.7/34.0.

record.verdict_notes: All baselines are recoverable from the subscripts, so 'not reliably aligned' is overstated, and the Table 3 rows can be added. The size effect is confounded: each size is a different Qwen3-VL base, and the base models alone show the same trends. A researcher could reasonably classify this study as T4, using scaling rhetorically to describe its own method. The V6 verdicts should be read as very weak evidence.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute; power-law fits and bottleneck conditions.
No small-run fits or predictions of substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or parameter/token optima.
No comparison of architectures at fixed parameter count.
Visual reasoning is evaluated, but the study does not test whether the same power-law form holds in another modality or training regime.
No pretraining-loss-to-downstream relationship or fitted predictive curve; only reported benchmark scores across three Genesis model sizes.
No fitted exponents or compute-optimal split, and no test of fit-method or setup dependence of those quantities.

relationships.condition: Genesis 4B→8B→32B on ZB-Sub, MathVista, MMMU, MMMU-Pro, EMMA, HallusionBench, MMStar, InfoVQA
relationships.reason: Scores rise monotonically with size in R1–R15 and R22–R30. This rests on only three base checkpoints with no fit, so it is weak support for a monotone trend, not for predictability.
relationships.display_finding: Scores increased monotonically across the three model sizes, including HallusionBench at 72.5→73.0→74.6, without a fitted or tested predictive scaling law.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Genesis 4B→8B→32B on ZB-Sub, MathVista, MMMU, MMMU-Pro, EMMA, HallusionBench, MMStar, InfoVQA
source_check.reason: Split the condition group: R1–R15 and R25–R30 support a monotone size trend; R22–R24 show only a small HallusionBench improvement, 72.5→73.0→74.6, warranting limits_scope under the partial-effect rule. Predictive scaling itself remains untested.

relationships.condition: LogicVista, and UNREAL Natural Science / Physics sub-scores (text, Table 3)
relationships.reason: LogicVista is flat from 4B to 8B (60.0→59.7) before rising at 32B (R16–R18). From the Table 3 text, UNREAL Nat.Sci (40.3→37.1) and Phys (28.4→26.5) fall from 8B to 32B.
relationships.display_finding: LogicVista changed from 60.0 at 4B to 59.7 at 8B before improving at 32B, while UNREAL natural science fell 40.3 to 37.1 and physics 28.4 to 26.5 from 8B to 32B.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: LogicVista, and UNREAL Natural Science / Physics sub-scores (text, Table 3)
source_check.reason: Table 1 confirms LogicVista 60.0→59.7→68.5 for R16–R18. Table 3 confirms Natural Science 32.3→40.3→37.1 and Physics & Engineering 15.7→28.4→26.5. These settings qualify an otherwise positive size trend.

relationships.reason: Scores fall with size, 16.8→15.2→14.4 (R19–R21). The base models are also non-monotone, so the decline may reflect the base checkpoints rather than scale.
relationships.display_finding: Scores declined from 16.8 to 15.2 to 14.4 as size increased, although nonmonotonic base-model performance complicates attributing the decline to scale.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.reason: R19–R21 confirm a reversed size trend, 16.8→15.2→14.4. Corresponding base scores are non-monotone, 15.0→10.8→16.0; the results do not isolate parameter count as the cause.

tranche.reason: The three Genesis sizes provide downstream scaling results in a new multimodal RL setting. This is a weak V6 test, without fitted scaling laws or prospective predictions.

source_check.notes: Only three Qwen3-VL initializations are compared; no fitted law, extrapolation test or uncertainty establishes downstream predictability. Appendix A.3 contains example pipeline prompts, which are not instructions to this checker.
